gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22, a 100 W three-port charger, gives only 45 W + 45 W with two ports in use (techtest.org), or that Anker's own US store today lists the Prime 100W A2688 at $45.99 as a pre-order shipping Nov 25 - Dec 5, 2026.
standout_why: Compared against thisUSB (best-usb-c-chargers and A2343 vs A2688), ComputingForGeeks, TechFromAlex, SpecsEveryday, SolderMag and Cadiens, all opened 2026-11-27. Between them they already state the two winning splits (Anker Prime 100W 65 + 35 W; UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port 65 + 30 W) and several losers (Satechi 100W 60 + 30 W, Anker 735 45 + 20 W, Anker Nano 70W 45 + 22.5 W, UGREEN Nexode 65W 45 + 20 W, Anker 725 45 + 18 W). None mentions the Baseus AH22 at all. None carries a dated maker-store price for today: thisUSB, SolderMag and Cadiens print no prices, ComputingForGeeks and TechFromAlex print rough ranges, and SpecsEveryday's prices are dated 2026-10-17 ($69.99 for the Anker). The angle is only partly delivered: I could price one model (the Anker) myself; the UGREEN and Baseus stores and Amazon blocked every read.
decides: It confirms the pick stays between the Anker Prime 100W A2688 (65 + 35 W, Anker's service page) and the UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port (65 + 30 W, as Cadiens and three other rival pages report). It removes the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 from the page: Michael Barton's techtest.org table gives 45 + 45 W with two ports, so it misses the 65 W line despite its 100 W label. On price, Anker's store is at $45.99 against a $69.99 list, with no sale end date stated and the unit on pre-order, so any 'Anker is cheaper' claim must carry both caveats. The UGREEN rows need their store prices re-read before the page ranks on price; the project's own record has them at $42.99 and $42.49, which I could not re-open.
